correctness.rationale: For the fixed known injection location/time, take p=1/D, q=v/D and A=log(M√p/√(4π)). This maps the physical domain bijectively to p,q>0 and A real; Y=log(C√t)=A−x²p/(4t)+xq/2−q²t/(4p). Differencing at the first time fixes q=ap+b, with a=(x₁+x₂)/(2t₁)>0 and b determined by the readings. Differencing across times at x₁ then gives γ=κp−2ab−b²/p. Exactly the positive roots satisfying ap+b>0 are physical: Y₁₁ fixes A freely, and the two differences then certify the other readings. For κ>0 the right-hand side is strictly increasing. For κ<0, choose b>0 and distinct positive p values with product b²/(−κ); then both slopes q are positive and the two time differences coincide. The resulting quadratic roots are simple and positive, persist with both inequalities strict under small changes of (Y₁₁,b,γ), and exhaust the fiber. Since these three data coordinates are invertible affine functions of the Y values, the double-fiber set is open also in positive concentrations. For κ=0, b=γ=0 makes every p>0 admissible at a fixed Y₁₁; this is an existence assertion, not a statement about every critical-design data triple. Taking positive square roots in κ>0 gives the exact sensor inequality, which imposes x₂<x₁ and t₂/t₁<4. For the rectangle, spatial slopes at two distinct times determine the slope and intercept of a line in 1/t: their difference uniquely fixes p since x₁+x₂>0, then q and A follow. The example can be replayed by inserting (p,q,A)=(1/2,7/4,0) and (8/7,19/7,−27/112) into Y; the ordered L readings are (−25/32,−9/32,−9/4) for both, with distinct fourth readings −25/16 and −37/28. RESULT.md §§1–5 establish global noiseless identification only. The finite rational verifier and its notes were inspected, not executed.

evidence: Ogata–Banks solve a semi-infinite forward problem with a prescribed inlet value and zero initial concentration. Browning et al.'s inspected passages describe a structural identifiability method based on differential algebra for partially observed PDEs.

The available bibliographic/abstract descriptions of the 2005 inverse study concern unknown source position and time-dependent intensity with time recordings. Its full text and the 2020 monitoring-design full text were not available in this review.

evidence: Even fixing release metadata and zero decay in the closest advective catalogue result leaves a substantially richer observation operator than the three mixed-time samples. The one-snapshot quadratic test instead requires all readings at a known age.
The decisive frozen comparison is the positivity and number of roots of κp²−(γ+2ab)p−b² with ap+b>0, not observability under arbitrary time histories.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Injectivity for richer data and a larger parameter space does not imply it survives deleting data, and noninjectivity for more unknowns need not survive fixing them. The checked statements do not settle this smaller measurement map and its exceptional geometries.

evidence: Gaussian logarithms make both the frozen inverse and nearby records algebraic. The single-snapshot Gaussian record imposes unisolvency for quadratics; the transient three-monitor record uses full traces or three times per station.
The frozen three samples instead require intersecting q=ap+b with the quadratic constraint involving q²/p; global fibers change when κ changes sign.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The single-snapshot model can absorb v into the unknown center at that time, but the L-data are not simultaneous; there is no transformation of the given three observations to a quadratic spatial interpolant at a common time. The full-trace sampling operator likewise is not an equivalent description of the L-design.

value.rationale: Two stations with one repeat measurement impose a natural sparse observation budget. The theorem decides whether noiseless global identification can even be attempted at that budget and separates unique, two-valued and continuous ambiguity, with an explicit fourth-reading remedy. The coupling of geometry and time, rather than just a local rank calculation or a count of unknowns, makes the exact boundary useful. It supplies neither noise conditioning nor field guidance beyond the ideal passive model.
